claim: Well-defined roles and interaction patterns among agents significantly increase task success rates in multi-agent systems.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by comparing task success rates in multi-agent systems with explicitly defined roles and interaction protocols versus systems without such structure, under controlled experimental conditions.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Well-defined roles and interaction–Task success rates principle

claim: Payload referencing reduces token generation overhead in inter-agent communication while improving goal success rate on code-intensive tasks.

conditions: LLM-based agents (Claude 3.5 Sonnet supervisor, Claude 3.0 Sonnet specialists)
